function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
There’s no definitive “greatest” because greatness depends on what you’re measuring—championships, individual skill, longevity, cultural impact, or how one changed the game. Here’s a quick snapshot of the most frequently cited candidates:

| Player | Era | Championships | MVPs / Finals MVPs | Key Strengths |
|--------|-----|---------------|--------------------|--------------|
| **Michael Jordan** | ’80‑’00 | 6 NBA titles (1991–96, 99‑2000) | 5 regular‑season MVPs, 6 Finals MVPs | Scoring prowess, defensive tenacity, clutch play, global brand |
| **LeBron James** | ’09‑present | 4 NBA titles (2012, 14, 16, 22) | 4 regular‑season MVPs, 4 Finals MVPs | Versatility (scorer + facilitator), durability, leadership across multiple franchises |
| **Kareem Abdul‑Jabbar** | ’70‑'90 | 6 NBA titles | 6 regular‑season MVPs, 2 Finals MVPs | All‑time leading scorer, unstoppable skyhook, longevity |
| **Magic Johnson** | ’80‑'95 | 5 NBA titles | 3 regular‑season MVPs, 3 Finals MVPs | Playmaking wizardry, versatility at point guard & forward |

### Why the debate stays alive

* **Statistical dominance:** Jordan led the league in scoring five times and had a career average of 30.12 ppg – still the highest among players with >10 seasons. LeBron has surpassed 38,000 points while maintaining near‑50% shooting efficiency over more than 20 years.
  
* **Championship pedigree:** Both have six rings each, though Jordan did it all with Chicago Bulls during two dominant dynasties, whereas LeBron won with three different teams, showing adaptability.

* **Cultural impact:** Jordan turned into a worldwide icon, launching Air Jordans and redefining sports marketing. LeBron leveraged his platform off‑court (education initiatives, political activism) and remains highly relevant today.

* **Versatility vs specialization:** Some argue LeBron’s ability to fill any role makes him superior in modern analytics terms, while others champion Jordan’s pure offensive firepower and defensive excellence.

Ultimately, many fans choose based on personal preference: *“I love the way he scored,”* versus *“He was everything.”* In short, both Jordan and LeBron are legitimate contenders for the title of greatest, and the conversation continues largely because they represent slightly different eras and styles of play.
